decisive_items: 2-week history of chest pain during exertion
Patient developed left bundle-branch block (LBBB) in stage 2 at heart rate of 107 beats per minute with chest pain
Coronary computed tomography angiography showed no abnormalities
response.rationale: Exertional angina with exercise-induced LBBB and normal coronary CTA best fits Cardiac Syndrome X/microvascular angina; obstructive CAD is excluded by normal CTA, and structural causes like HCM are less supported by a normal baseline ECG and lack of other features.

rejected.why: Vasospastic angina typically causes rest pain with transient ST elevation; here pain is consistently exertional and resolves with rest.
Coronary artery disease is contradicted by the normal coronary CTA.
Aortic stenosis would require valvular/murmur/echo evidence, which is not provided, and normal baseline ECG makes it unlikely.
Mitral valve prolapse is not associated with this exertional LBBB and chest pain pattern, and no supporting features are present.
